title: An Evaluation of the Pedagogical Soundness and Usability of AI-Generated Lesson Plans Across Different Models and Prompt Frameworks in High-School Physics
extended_summary:
This paper examines whether AI-generated lesson plans are pedagogically sound and usable for classroom instruction, with a focus on high-school physics. The central question is not student learning impact, but how lesson-plan quality varies across large language models and structured prompting approaches, especially in terms of readability, factual accuracy, curriculum alignment, and cognitive demand.

The study generated fifteen lesson plans for a single topic, The Electromagnetic Spectrum, using five LLMs (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, DeepSeek, and Grok) crossed with three prompt frameworks (TAG, RACE, and COSTAR). The plans were created for mixed-ability Grades 9–12 classrooms and then evaluated with automated metrics measuring readability, hallucination/factual errors, NGSS alignment, and Bloom’s taxonomy level. No human participants were involved as intervention recipients; the paper evaluates model outputs rather than classroom implementation.

The findings suggest that model choice most strongly affected readability, while prompt framework structure mattered more for factual completeness and incidental standards alignment. RACE generally produced the best factual and curricular results, while DeepSeek produced the most accessible language. Across all models and prompts, objectives clustered at lower Bloom’s levels, with few higher-order objectives. The paper concludes that effective lesson planning with generative AI requires careful model selection, structured prompts, and explicit instructional checklists to improve completeness and pedagogical quality.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI's GPT-based conversational large language model/chatbot used for generating text outputs such as lesson plans.
identified_tools.use_case: Used to generate AI lesson plans for the high-school physics topic The Electromagnetic Spectrum under TAG, RACE, and COSTAR prompts; also used to refine Python code snippets.

findings.finding_summary: ChatGPT-generated lesson plans showed moderate readability (mean FKGL=10.86; mean FRE=41.73) and moderate incidental NGSS alignment (mean 0.063). Cognitive objectives were concentrated at lower Bloom levels (CDI=2.294), and the paper reports no factual inaccuracies but some omissions reflected in a Hallucination Index of 2.50.
findings.measure: Readability, hallucination/omission index, NGSS similarity, Bloom-level cognitive demand

identified_tools.name: Claude
identified_tools.description: Anthropic's Claude family of conversational large language models used for generating text outputs such as lesson plans.
identified_tools.use_case: Used to generate AI lesson plans for the high-school physics topic The Electromagnetic Spectrum under TAG, RACE, and COSTAR prompts.

findings.finding_summary: Claude-generated lesson plans were the least readable among the models (mean FKGL=19.89; mean FRE=9.89) but had the highest incidental NGSS similarity (mean 0.110). The paper reports no factual inaccuracies, but Claude had omissions reflected in a Hallucination Index of 2.67, and objectives remained mostly lower-order (CDI=2.262).
findings.measure: Readability, hallucination/omission index, NGSS similarity, Bloom-level cognitive demand

identified_tools.name: Gemini
identified_tools.description: Google's Gemini family of conversational large language models used for generating text outputs such as lesson plans.
identified_tools.use_case: Used to generate AI lesson plans for the high-school physics topic The Electromagnetic Spectrum under TAG, RACE, and COSTAR prompts.

findings.finding_summary: Gemini-generated lesson plans had moderate readability (mean FKGL=11.03; mean FRE=43.44) and moderate NGSS similarity (mean 0.061). The paper reports no factual inaccuracies, but omissions produced a Hallucination Index of 2.33, and the objectives were concentrated at low Bloom levels (CDI=1.578).
findings.measure: Readability, hallucination/omission index, NGSS similarity, Bloom-level cognitive demand

identified_tools.name: DeepSeek
identified_tools.description: DeepSeek's conversational large language model used for generating text outputs such as lesson plans.
identified_tools.use_case: Used to generate AI lesson plans for the high-school physics topic The Electromagnetic Spectrum under TAG, RACE, and COSTAR prompts.

findings.finding_summary: DeepSeek produced the most readable plans (mean FKGL=8.64; mean FRE=54.65), but also had the highest Hallucination Index among the models (2.83), indicating more omissions. Its mean NGSS similarity was 0.061, and objective cognitive demand remained low (CDI=2.193).
findings.measure: Readability, hallucination/omission index, NGSS similarity, Bloom-level cognitive demand

identified_tools.name: Grok
identified_tools.description: xAI's Grok conversational large language model used for generating text outputs such as lesson plans.
identified_tools.use_case: Used to generate AI lesson plans for the high-school physics topic The Electromagnetic Spectrum under TAG, RACE, and COSTAR prompts.

findings.finding_summary: Grok had the strongest factual reliability on the paper's hallucination metric (mean HI=2.00), but its readability was less accessible than DeepSeek's (mean FKGL=13.32; mean FRE=29.47). Its NGSS similarity was 0.092, and cognitive demand remained low (CDI=1.780).
findings.measure: Readability, hallucination/omission index, NGSS similarity, Bloom-level cognitive demand

quality_tier_rationale: This is a single descriptive/computational evaluation of generated lesson plans, not a causal study, RCT, or meta-analysis. It reports no field deployment, repeated-use teacher adoption, or outcome effects on students or teachers.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper shows modest evidence of pedagogical limitations and variability in generated lesson plans, but it does not estimate a causal impact size on instructional outcomes. Findings are useful for screening usability, readability, and hallucination risk, but overall impact on K-12 practice is unclear.
